newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC warns right-wingers after army raid.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC warns right-wingers after army raid.

text.p: A prominent South African right-winger was among 12 people arrested on Monday for breaking into an army base, prompting the black majority African National Congress to issue a warning to pro-apartheid forces.
Police said white right-winger Willem Ratte and 11 people were arrested at 3 a.m. (0100 GMT) inside the Pomfret military base, a restricted area, in North West region.

"The 12 suspects, including a woman and a 16-year-old boy, were arrested inside the Pomfret military base and are being held on charges of attempted sabotage and housebreaking. We are investigating," police inspector Rina Matthysen told Reuters.
They are all being held in police custody pending a court hearing, due within 48 hours of their arrest.
Commending their swift arrest by police, the ruling ANC warned in a statement it would not tolerate threats to South Africa's hard-won democracy.

"If the sinister forces that are hell-bent on drowning the democratic dispensation in blood have not yet learnt their lesson, then (these) arrests should send a clear message that no-one will be allowed to act with impunity," the ANC said.
Ratte is currently out on bail pending his appeal against a five-year sentence for his participation in the seizure of an old fort in Pretoria three years ago.

He won his release on bail after being on a hunger strike which lasted for 54 days last year. The ruling ANC however has attacked the hunger strike as "phony", saying Ratte had taken nourishing fluids.

Ratte also clashed with police in 1995 when he holed himself up at a farm outside Pretoria to guard the transmitter for a right-wing radio station, which had been broadcasting illegally for nine months.

Two white extremists, Cliff Barnard and Abraham Myburgh, were jailed for 50 years each on Friday for their part in four bombings aimed at derailing 1994 all-race polls which brought the ANC to power. A third co-accused, Jan de Wet, was jailed for 25 years.
All three were caught in January this year, a month after four people died in a bombing claimed by a little-known white right-wing group.
President Nelson Mandela's ANC said in their statement that although white right-wingers were a minority, they could not be ignored.
"We hope that the courts will take due regard of the threat they potentially pose to the country," the ruling party said.
